---
title: "Figure 6.1: Headline Consumer Price Inflation"
---

![Python: `python/fig-6-1.py`](../images/python/fig-6-1.png)

Monthly inflation for five economies up to the latest data, followed by a
dotted line to each economy's end-2026 projection, marked with a dot.

**New in this chart:**

- splitting each series into actual data and a projection;
- the lines starting at the left edge;
- a two-column legend in row order.

## The data

Sheet `data`, 204 rows of monthly data from 2010. The columns are LA7, CAPDR,
CARIB, USA and CAN, plus helper columns LA7\* ... CAN\* that Excel uses for
the projection markers.

Each series has values up to its latest month and then a gap. December 2026
holds the projection.

## The script

### The period

```python
START, END = pd.Timestamp("2024-01-01"), pd.Timestamp("2026-12-31")
...
# Include December 2023, so the lines run in from the left edge as in Excel.
data = data[(data["category"] >= "2023-12-01") & (data["category"] <= END)]
```

The x-axis starts in January 2024. If the data started there too, the lines
would begin a little inside the plot, because the monthly values are dated at
the end of the month. Keeping December 2023 and cutting it off at the axis
makes the lines run in from the left edge, as in the published chart.

### Actual data, the dotted link and the projection

```python
for series, colour in series_colours.items():
    values = data.set_index("category")[series].dropna()
    actual, projection = values.iloc[:-1], values.iloc[-1:]
```

For each economy:

1. **Dates as the index.** `set_index("category")` makes the dates the
   *index* of the table, the labels of its rows. The selected column then
   carries its dates with it.
2. **Drop the gap.** `dropna()` removes the empty months, so only the actual
   values and the projection are left.
3. **Split.** The last remaining value is the projection (`iloc[-1:]`, the
   last row) and everything before it is actual data (`iloc[:-1]`).

```python
    ax.plot(actual.index, actual, color=colour, linewidth=1.8,
            solid_capstyle="round", label=series)
    ax.plot([actual.index[-1], projection.index[0]],
            [actual.iloc[-1], projection.iloc[0]],
            color=colour, linewidth=1.8, linestyle=(0, (1, 1.5)))
    ax.scatter(projection.index, projection, s=70, color=colour,
               edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.8, zorder=3, clip_on=False)
```

Three pieces are drawn per economy:

- **the actual data**, as a solid line;
- **a dotted line** from the latest actual month to the projection, made of
  just two points;
- **the projection**, as a dot with a black outline.

The dots sit exactly on the right edge of the plot. `clip_on=False` keeps
their right half from being cut off.

### Labels and axes

```python
ax.text(END, 5.55, "End-2026\nprojections", fontsize=9, fontstyle="italic",
        ha="right", va="center", linespacing=1.0)

ax.set_xticks(pd.to_datetime([
    "2024-01-31", "2024-07-31", "2025-01-31", "2025-07-31",
    "2026-01-31", "2026-07-31", "2026-12-31",
]))
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%b-%y"))
```

The tick dates are listed one by one. They are every six months, plus
December 2026 for the projections, which no regular `date_range` would
produce.

### The legend

```python
# Two-column legend, read row by row: LA7, CAPDR / CARIB, USA / CAN.
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
order = [0, 2, 4, 1, 3]
ax.legend([handles[i] for i in order], [labels[i] for i in order],
          loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.03, 1.0), ncol=2,
          handlelength=2.6, labelspacing=0.1, columnspacing=1.5)
```

matplotlib fills legend columns from top to bottom. To get Excel's row order
(LA7 and CAPDR on the first row), the entries are passed in the order 0, 2,
4 (left column) and 1, 3 (right column). Compare the more general solution in
[Figure 2.3](fig-2-3.qmd).

## The complete script

The full `python/fig-6-1.py`, as it runs:

```` {.python filename="python/fig-6-1.py"}
"""Figure 6.1: Headline Consumer Price Inflation."""
import matplotlib.dates as mdates
import pandas as pd

from chart_style import new_chart, read_chart_data, save_chart, set_y_scale

STEM = "fig-6-1"

START, END = pd.Timestamp("2024-01-01"), pd.Timestamp("2026-12-31")
CONFLICT = pd.Timestamp("2026-03-01")

data = read_chart_data(STEM)
# Include December 2023, so the lines run in from the left edge as in Excel.
data = data[(data["category"] >= "2023-12-01") & (data["category"] <= END)]

series_colours = {
    "LA7": "#5B267D",
    "CAPDR": "#C45A12",
    "CARIB": "#08A7B5",
    "USA": "#0067A6",
    "CAN": "#666666",
}

fig, ax = new_chart(
    title="Headline Consumer Price Inflation",
    subtitle="(Year-over-year percent change)",
    caption=(
        "Sources: Haver Analytics; IMF, World Economic Outlook database;\n"
        "national authorities; and IMF staff calculations.\n"
        "Note: Aggregates are purchasing-power-parity GDP-weighted averages.\n"
        "CAPDR = Central America, Panama, and the Dominican Republic; CARIB\n"
        "= Caribbean; LA7 = Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Paraguay, Peru,\n"
        "Uruguay."
    ),
    left=0.3,
    right=0.25,
    bottom_gap=0.5,
)

# Each series holds monthly data up to its latest month, then a gap, then the
# end-2026 projection in December 2026. The monthly data are drawn as a solid
# line; a dotted line joins the latest month to the projection, which is
# marked with a dot.
for series, colour in series_colours.items():
    values = data.set_index("category")[series].dropna()
    actual, projection = values.iloc[:-1], values.iloc[-1:]
    ax.plot(actual.index, actual, color=colour, linewidth=1.8,
            solid_capstyle="round", label=series)
    ax.plot([actual.index[-1], projection.index[0]],
            [actual.iloc[-1], projection.iloc[0]],
            color=colour, linewidth=1.8, linestyle=(0, (1, 1.5)))
    ax.scatter(projection.index, projection, s=70, color=colour,
               edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.8, zorder=3, clip_on=False)

ax.axvline(CONFLICT, color="black", linewidth=0.6, linestyle=(0, (1, 1.5)))
ax.text(CONFLICT - pd.Timedelta(days=10), 1.08, "Middle East conflict",
        fontsize=9, fontstyle="italic", ha="right", va="bottom")
ax.text(END, 5.55, "End-2026\nprojections", fontsize=9, fontstyle="italic",
        ha="right", va="center", linespacing=1.0)

ax.set_xlim(START, END)
ax.set_xticks(pd.to_datetime([
    "2024-01-31", "2024-07-31", "2025-01-31", "2025-07-31",
    "2026-01-31", "2026-07-31", "2026-12-31",
]))
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%b-%y"))
ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=90, length=2.8)

set_y_scale(ax, 1, 6, 1)
ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=2.8)

# Two-column legend, read row by row: LA7, CAPDR / CARIB, USA / CAN.
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
order = [0, 2, 4, 1, 3]
ax.legend([handles[i] for i in order], [labels[i] for i in order],
          loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.03, 1.0), ncol=2,
          handlelength=2.6, labelspacing=0.1, columnspacing=1.5)

save_chart(fig, STEM)
````
